handoff.summary: Phase 5 (Review and recovery) is complete. P05-T05 adds the machine-first draftforge review command, persisted reviewer leases and crash reconciliation, bounded repair attempts against retained worktrees, merge-on-accept integration with a durable rollback point, reported usage enforcement, CLI/status summaries, and deterministic failure and dependency fixtures. Independent Terra QA rejected the first ignored-directory secret-scan repair until recursive traversal was bounded by depth, entry count, file count, per-file bytes, and aggregate bytes; switched to incremental enumeration; and gained canonical path plus device/inode identity checks across the full ancestor chain and opened file descriptor. The final independent verdict is ACCEPT. The integrated gate is green on macOS: 466 tests, 461 pass, 0 fail, 5 expected environment skips, with typecheck, lint, session check, build, git diff check, and built CLI run/review/resume/status fixtures passing. Phase 6 (Release) is next. The reviewer 'block' verdict over passing machine evidence still maps to classification 'unknown'; changing that provisional decision requires amending ADR 0010.
decisionsLocked: Use strict TypeScript, Node.js, npm, and ESM.
Route architect, worker, and reviewer roles through provider adapters with configurable model IDs.
Use .draftforge/state.json as canonical state and generate SESSION.md from it.
Use DAG task contracts, isolated workers, and independent review before completion.
Serialize task transitions with a project lock and append redacted events before atomic snapshot writes.
Apply optional config.local.json as a deep override, then validate the merged configuration.
Store resumable interview drafts and revision-bound approval in .draftforge/planning.json while keeping runnable task state authoritative in .draftforge/state.json.
Materialize approved phase, ADR, and task files before making active-phase roots ready.
Accept exactly one architect envelope per turn and derive the expected kind from planning state.
Parse raw model text in src/application/ and validate it before it reaches domain state.
Drive planning through plan --prompt, --submit, and --answer until Phase 3 adapters exist.
Change an approved plan only through a recorded revision that carries answers forward and preserves recorded progress.
Retain one superseded plan so re-materialization can tell generated files from user edits.

Decompose Phase 3 by transport: shared runner/reliability foundation (P03-T01), harness adapters (P03-T02), API adapters (P03-T03), then doctor auth and plan wiring (P03-T04), with every adapter passing one reusable contract-test suite.
Adapters map transport failures to AdapterError with a correct retryable flag; the runner centralizes timeout, retry, and redaction so authentication and contract errors are never retried.
Codex CLI and Claude Code share an injectable shell-free child-process transport; prompts use stdin, provider-default omits the model flag, and explicit models are forwarded.

OpenAI and Anthropic share an injectable fetch transport (no vendor SDK); keys come from the environment only, provider-default resolves to a default model constant in the provider layer, and HTTP 401/403 are terminal while 429 and 5xx are transient.
The live API smoke tests require both the provider key and DRAFTFORGE_LIVE_SMOKE=1 so a routine npm run check never issues a paid request by surprise.
Drive one provider-backed architect turn with plan --run; keep plan --prompt and plan --submit as unchanged manual checkpoints.
Doctor checks only configured role adapters, caches duplicate routes, treats absent authentication as missing, and never surfaces environment values or subprocess output.

On Windows, preserve where.exe PATH order, ignore unsupported extensionless aliases, spawn executables directly, and invoke npm-style .cmd/.bat shims through an escaped cmd.exe boundary while prompts remain on stdin.

Represent every worker dispatch with a stable attempt reference in canonical task state and a schema-validated manifest under .draftforge/runs; claim under the project lock, then release it before workspace or model side effects.
Treat workflow.currentTask as a display pointer only; task statuses and attempt references are the authoritative set of concurrent work.

Use the task file referenced by canonical state as the execution contract, record its hash per attempt, normalize segment-aware path ownership, and reserve canonical state, SESSION.md, and run-control artifacts to the scheduler.
Create deterministic Git worktrees under the run directory, preserve uncertain work, and resume the same attempt/worktree instead of transparently retrying a side-effecting worker call.
Phase 4 workspace mutation is available only through workspace-capable local harness adapters; text-only API worker routes fail before claim until a separate patch/tool protocol is designed.
Worker success advances only to review. Independent acceptance, repairs, merges, rollback, secret scanning, and usage accounting remain Phase 5.

Decompose Phase 4 by concern: execution contracts and scheduling (P04-T01) plus Git workspace isolation (P04-T02) can proceed in parallel; worker execution/evidence (P04-T03) joins them; run/resume and the exit gate finish in P04-T04.

Treat every worker-mutable Git control surface as untrusted during inspection: use fixed safe command overrides, reject executable filters and tracked submodules, and preserve any workspace whose authoritative scope cannot be proven.

Review is machine-first: DraftForge runs the contract's verification commands, the scope check, and the secret scan itself, and acceptance requires both passing machine evidence and an accept verdict. A model verdict may reject what passed but can never accept what failed.

Verification commands run in the attempt worktree through the shell-free boundary and only in an allowlisted shape (npm run <script>, node <path> with literal arguments); anything else is a contract violation that blocks rather than a check that is skipped.
A secret detection records only rule id, path, and line number - never the value, a substring of it, or surrounding context - because evidence files get committed and shared.
Failure classification is a closed taxonomy stored durably on the task, and only verification-failure and review-rejection are repairable; everything else blocks on first occurrence.
Repair is bounded by limits.maxRepairAttempts, returns review -> active against the same worktree with findings carried into the prompt, and automation never leaves blocked on its own.

Acceptance integrates: scope and secrets are re-checked, the project branch head is recorded as a rollback point, the attempt branch is merged from a clean project root, and only then does the task reach done. Rollback stays documented guidance, not automation.
Usage accounting is reported, never estimated: unpriced models and harness adapters record unknown, and an exceeded declared budget refuses the call rather than truncating work.

Repay the two Phase 4 debts as the Phase 5 foundation (P05-T01): the project lock waits with bounded retry, DispatchGate is deleted, and the worker seam accepts a running manifest so resume stops rewinding one.

Decompose Phase 5 as foundation first (P05-T01), then three path-disjoint parallel tasks - verification and secret scanning (P05-T02), reviewer prompt and verdict (P05-T03), usage accounting (P05-T04) - then the review command, repair loop, integration, and exit gate (P05-T05).
Serialize only durable review claims and state transitions; never hold the project lock across verification, secret scanning, a reviewer or worker model call, or a Git merge.
Persist a reviewer lease and integration intent before their external side effects so crash recovery neither calls a reviewer twice nor merges accepted work twice.

Treat ignored untracked trees as untrusted input: enumerate incrementally with hard entry, file, depth, and byte caps, and bind every traversal step to canonical path plus device/inode identity before content enters secret scanning or reviewer context.
openQuestions: Should a reviewer block verdict over passing machine evidence keep the terminal unknown classification, or should ADR 0010 add a dedicated taxonomy value?
nextActions: Open Phase 6 (Release): record any release-specific ADRs, define its task DAG, and make only the approved roots ready.

Still open from Phase 4: drive a successful multi-task parallel dispatch through the built CLI with a real codex-cli or claude-cli. Phase 4 proved this with deterministic fake runners only, and no harness is installed in this shell.
Decide whether reviewer block over passing machine evidence needs a dedicated ADR 0010 classification before the release contract is frozen.
gotchas: `withProjectLock` now waits rather than refusing: one deadline is computed at entry (DEFAULT_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS 30s, DEFAULT_LOCK_POLL_INTERVAL_MS 25ms, both overridable per call) and every transient condition retries via the internal RetryableLockContention signal. Stale locks are still broken immediately. If you add a new refusal path in lock.ts, make it retryable unless it is genuinely unrecoverable - a hard throw there silently reintroduces the contention refusal.
Two concurrent `draftforge run` processes now wait for each other instead of one failing. That is a deliberate behavior change from Phase 4 and P05-T05 must document it in the CLI docs.

The worker seam accepts exactly two entry shapes: `claimed` with `baseCommit: null`, or `running` with a non-null base commit that must equal the recovered workspace's. Any other lifecycle, or a resumed base-commit mismatch, is a hard error before side effects - do not soften the mismatch into an overwrite.
`blocked -> ready` requires actorKind `human`; automation calling it throws. transitionTask defaults to `automation`, so a reopen must pass it explicitly.
TaskState.review is a required field (nullable), so every literal TaskState construction needs it - including test fixtures. Missing it is a compile error, not a migration concern.
`run` reports an interrupted attempt as in-flight and leaves it alone; only `resume` re-dispatches it. This reading of the P04-T04 contract is documented in README and docs/PROTOCOL.md.

Execution fixtures are a deterministic builder (`node --import tsx test/fixtures/execution/project.ts <variant> <dir>`, variants unapproved/api-worker/deferred/resumable/no-work), not committed static directories.

Workspace scope enforcement must stay content-derived: tracked changes come from a scratch index (no stat cache) unioned with a `--cached` diff. Reverting to a plain `git diff <base>` silently reopens a Windows hole where a same-size, restored-mtime rewrite is invisible; test/workspaces/git.test.ts guards it.
Changed paths now include a staged change whose worktree edit was reverted. This over-reporting is deliberate and safe; do not 'fix' it by dropping the `--cached` diff.

Recorded green evidence is environment-specific: P04-T01..T03 were marked done from a green run whose commit then failed 7 tests on a Windows machine. Commit 09a2943 has since been re-verified green on macOS (242 pass, 5 skips), so HEAD is trustworthy on both, but re-run `npm run check` locally rather than trusting a recorded run from another platform.
`templates/schema/*.json` must stay byte-identical to `.draftforge/schema/*.json`; test/templates.test.ts enforces it.
P04-T01 adds a shipped execution schema and changes state/planning contracts; runtime validators, migrations, fixtures, and template copies must move together.
P04-T01 and P04-T02 are intentionally path-disjoint and ready together. Canonical state, SESSION.md, and `.draftforge/runs/` are lead/scheduler control paths, not worker-owned paths.
A worker model call can mutate its worktree, so provider-level transparent retry must be disabled for that call; timeout or transient failure is resumed explicitly against the same attempt.
Phase 4 must not mark worker output done. Its dependency test may simulate a trusted reviewer transition, but real reviewer execution starts in Phase 5.
API adapters remain usable for text-only roles, but Phase 4 run/resume must reject an API-backed worker route before claiming work because no safe patch/tool protocol exists yet.
The default model IDs live in `src/providers/api/openai-api.ts` and `anthropic-api.ts` (DEFAULT_MODEL); update them there when a provider's default moves — config and domain must not pin a model ID.

Codex CLI, Claude Code, and provider API keys were not detected in this shell; provider live smoke tests require DRAFTFORGE_LIVE_SMOKE=1 plus the corresponding available authentication and otherwise skip.
Windows npm-installed harnesses may resolve through .cmd shims; keep process invocation escaping and PATH-order regression tests intact.
Generated `.draftforge/runs/` events are ignored run artifacts and must not be staged.

Worker Git inspection fails closed for executable clean/process filters, mutable fsmonitor or hook configuration, unsafe index/history/exclusion controls, tracked submodules, and local/worktree line-ending normalization overrides; P04-T04 CLI documentation must surface these limitations actionably.
A timeout whose child or descendants are not definitely terminated records the PID but leaves the task active and skips workspace inspection; resume must prove process absence before reuse.
An approved plan is still immutable in place: plan --submit and plan --prompt refuse it until `plan --revise` starts a recorded revision.
The architect prompt text is asserted in test/architect.test.ts; changing wording means updating those assertions.
If a process crashes during the brief stale-lock recovery claim, verify no DraftForge process is running before removing `.draftforge/state.lock.recovery`.
The workspace is OneDrive-backed, so large file operations can be slower than normal.

P05-T01 owns both carried Phase 4 debts (the refusing lock plus DispatchGate, and the resume-time manifest rewind). Do not fix either one from another task; they are that contract's acceptance criteria.

Integration requires a clean project working tree. A session with uncommitted local edits will defer acceptance rather than merge over them, which is deliberate - do not relax it into a stash-and-merge.

State schema 3 must migrate from both 1 and 2, and `.draftforge/schema/*.json` must stay byte-identical to `templates/schema/*.json` (test/templates.test.ts enforces it). Validators, migration, fixtures, and both schema copies move together.
The reviewer role is text-only, so unlike the worker role it works on API adapters and may use transparent retry; a reviewer call has no workspace side effects.
config already ships `roles.reviewer` and `limits.maxRepairAttempts`, so Phase 5 needs no config schema change - read the existing limits rather than adding new ones.

Secret-scan tests must plant synthetic credentials only, and must assert the value never appears in findings, events, or evidence. A test that prints what it planted defeats the invariant it is guarding.
`draftforge review` reconciles persisted worker results before filtering review tasks, and a persisted verdict is reused rather than calling the reviewer again.
A short-lived durable reviewer lease prevents concurrent review processes from duplicating a model call; stale ownership is recovered only after process liveness is disproven.
Integration intent is written before merge. Recovery accepts an already-merged branch tip, but refuses when the project branch has advanced away from the recorded rollback point.

Ignored untracked directories are secret-scanned recursively but fail closed above depth 32, 1,024 entries, 1,024 files, 1 MiB per file, or 8 MiB aggregate. Incremental enumeration and ancestor/file identity checks prevent resource exhaustion and symlink-swap substitution.
